messages:
maria (platform PM): heads up — proposal to add a lightweight consent prompt when a service account from a different org/project is used via the console or API. aim: make attribution + quota decisions explicit.
aj (eng): +1. do you mean the console UX only or also the token exchange/APIs?
sara (security): both. we should warn about cross-org privileges and require an explicit opt-in. simple checkbox is fine.
liam (infra): from infra side we need a deterministic attribution signal for billing/quotas. current flow loses the actor->sa mapping when tokens are exchanged. example header we could add: `X-Redwood-Impersonate: sa:projects/42@org-acme` and `X-Redwood-Acting-For: user:alice@org-foo`
ben (billing): that's useful. for billing we need to know whether to charge the caller org or the SA's org. leaning toward caller org by default but allow SA project override with consent.
maria (platform PM): UX idea: show a small consent banner in console and a `consent=true` query param for programmatic flows. default to caller attribution unless `consent` set and SA owner has allowed cross-charge. also list which metrics will be visible to which org.
aj (eng): implementation nit: if we add `consent=true` we must sign it server-side; clients can fake it. recommend a signed consent token issued by SA owner: `POST /v1/sa/consent -> {signed_consent_token}`. then callers include `X-SA-Consent: <token>` when exchanging.
sara (security): agree — signed token good. TTL short (24h), aud claim. also audit-log every exchange and surface in console under SA -> "Recent Delegations".
liam (infra): telemetry fields proposal (for infra/observability): `attribution.source = caller_project`, `attribution.service_account = sa_project`, `attribution.consent = signed|implicit|none`. that lets us roll up token-level cost and still debug edge cases.
ben (billing): please ensure `attribution.amount_units` and `attribution.reason` are included downstream to billing export so we can summarize chargebacks.
maria (platform PM): ok for rollout: start behind a feature-flag for Dedicated + Private, validate telemetry for 2 weeks, then soft-enforce UI prompt for Hosted. can we sketch migration steps?
aj (eng): plan: (1) add signed consent endpoint and DB table (sa_consents), (2) wire token exchange to require `X-SA-Consent` when `sa_project != caller_project` and `consent_required=true` feature flag, (3) add headers for attribution to internal router and propagate to billing pipeline. low risk if flagged.
liam (infra): fallback behavior: if consent required but missing, router should 403 with clear error: `SA_DELEGATION_CONSENT_REQUIRED`. avoid silent attribution flips.
sara (security): add a policy check UI so SA owners can pre-approve a set of trusted caller orgs — reduces UX friction for recurring cross-org calls.
maria (platform PM): sounds good. next steps: aj to prototype consent token API + example curl, liam to add telemetry fields to schema, sara to draft security UX copy, ben to validate billing export mapping. I'll file a console ticket and update rollout doc.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: auth-service v3.12 -> staging (consent-api feature flag enabled) :rocket:
aj (eng): quick prototype curl for review: 
```
# get signed consent (must be called by SA owner)
curl -X POST \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SA_OWNER_TOKEN" \ 
  -d '{"caller_project":"projects/99","expires_in":86400}' \ 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/sa/consent

# caller exchanges with consent
curl -X POST \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CALLER_TOKEN" \ 
  -H "X-SA-Consent: <signed_consent_token>" \ 
  -d '{"impersonate":"projects/42"}' \ 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/oauth/exchange
```
maria (platform PM): perfect — thanks everyone, file PRs against the feature branch and let's sync tomorrow 11am. :thumbsup:
